subject: Re: AtlasEdge migration proposal — structured migration credit & rollback protections
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Alexei Novak <alexei@atlasedge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AtlasEdge migration proposal — structured migration credit & rollback protections

Alexei —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation, I put together a short, high-level approach so AtlasEdge can evaluate the migration economics without increasing operational risk:

• Tiered migration credit: upfront pilot credit (first 3 months), then step-down credits tied to verified traffic migration milestones.
• Rollback protection: 45-day rollback window with a partial credit refund if critical runtime regressions prevent go-live (defined in runbook).
• SLA & performance fence: we’ll guarantee median p95 latency threshold for the pilot; if we miss by >25% across two consecutive weeks, AtlasEdge can pause migration and trigger engineering remediation.
• Onboarding hours & success playbook: we’ve budgeted 40 onboarding hours (included) and an optional extended onboarding block.

I attached the initial econ workbook and the high-level runbook we referenced: atlasedge-econ-proposal.xlsx; runbook-summary.pdf.

If you can share any procurement-specific constraints (contract term, required invoicing schedule, or an internal target for TCO reduction), we’ll map this to a final credit schedule.

Proposed next step: a brief call Thursday to agree on the credit schedule and the rollback acceptance criteria. Can you do 10–10:30am PT?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.com

--

Attachment: runbook-summary.pdf (PDF, 280KB)

From: Alexei Novak <alexei@atlasedge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Carter <emily@atlasedge.com>, procurements@atlasedge.com
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasEdge migration proposal — structured migration credit & rollback protections

Hannah —

Appreciate the write-up and attachments. A few clarifying points from our side:

1) Procurement is asking for a maximum credit cap and a clear clawback mechanism if we don’t hit migration milestones. They want the commercial commitments to be budget-neutral in year one.
2) We need stronger rollback protections for PII-heavy workloads — any guarantee that data pathways remain segregated during the rollback?
3) The 40 onboarding hours seem tight given our custom runtime integration; can we get a line item for an optional 80-hour block at a discounted rate?

I’ve attached a short doc with procurement questions they asked: procurement-questions.docx.

We like the 45-day window concept but would prefer the rollback period be tied to the go-live date for each segment (rather than a global window). Also — can you provide an explicit breakdown of how credits are applied to invoices and whether they are returned as cash or as account credit? That’s a procurement must-have.

I’m available Thursday but can do 11am PT instead of 10.

Thanks,
Alexei Novak
Head of Platform Engineering
AtlasEdge
alexei@atlasedge.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>

Alexei — thanks for the specific asks. I’ve updated the approach below to address procurement and engineering concerns. Quoted your points inline.

> 1) Procurement is asking for a maximum credit cap and a clear clawback mechanism if we don’t hit migration milestones.

We can include a hard credit cap for the pilot + onboarding phase and a clawback tied to measurable migration milestones (percentage of seats live by date). Clawback is applied as an invoice credit reversal over the following billing cycle — we do not issue cash refunds for migration credits; credits reduce future invoice balances unless otherwise negotiated at legal review.

> 2) We need stronger rollback protections for PII-heavy workloads — any guarantee that data pathways remain segregated during the rollback?

Engineering confirms we can enforce separate VPC peering paths and ephemeral routing during the rollback window; I’ve asked Marcus to review data-path controls and propose wording for the appendix.

> 3) The 40 onboarding hours seem tight given our custom runtime integration; can we get a line item for an optional 80-hour block at a discounted rate?

Yes — attached is credit-schedule-v2.xlsx with a second row for an 80-hour extended onboarding block at a 20% discount. The filing shows how extended hours convert to billable credits vs prepaid service.

Proposed updated milestone structure (short):
• Pilot credit: 50% credit on first 3 months up to $75k (cap).
• Stage 1 (25% traffic live): additional 25% credit applied to month 4 invoice.
• Stage 2 (75% traffic live): final 25% credit applied as account credit over next 2 invoices.
• Clawback: credits prorated and reversed if Stage 2 not achieved within 6 months.

Next steps: call Thursday 11am PT to align on cap and rollback appendix. I’ll bring Marcus for the data-path confirmation and Laura for commercial terms.

Best,
Hannah

--
